how:
First cut. Record the row on the way OUT of resolve() whether the resolver returned or raised, so the record is written by the frame rather than by the success path — the same shape harbor_master's clearance door uses for exactly this reason (a writer at the frame cannot miss a refusal nobody has thought of yet). The refused row carries the exception type and its message, cost 0, and a marker distinguishing it from an answer.

TWO THINGS THE BUILD MUST SETTLE FIRST, both named in the cast rather than assumed: WHICH raises earn a row (BadRequest fires before anything is spent and may not deserve one), and whether the row shape passes db_domain's existing write door unchanged. Both are read off the code at build time.

AND THE THIRD FALSIFIER CLAUSE IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, not an afterthought: a refusal must never be served back as a cache HIT. Recording a failure inside a store whose purpose is replaying stored answers is where this fix could end up worse than the defect.
